item.title: Shirahige Shrine: The Floating Torii of Lake Biwa — Guide
item.description: Shirahige Shrine, said to be nearly 1,900 years old and the head shrine of some 300 Shirahige shrines nationwide, is famous for its vermilion torii rising directly from the shallows of Lake Biwa — an image so reminiscent of Miyajima that the spot is called the ‘Itsukushima of Omi’. The shrine venerates a white-bearded god of longevity, and its lakeside halls climb the wooded slope behind, but the great moment is dawn, when the sun lifts over the lake’s far shore and the gate floats in a path of gold, mist and morning birdsong.
